structure.title: A death among colleagues
structure.text: The opening shows how other people receive Ivan's death before returning to the life that led there.

structure.title: A life re-examined
structure.text: Career, marriage, and illness bring accepted standards of success into an increasingly intimate examination.

people.name: Ivan Ilyich
people.text: A successful, correct and thoroughly ordinary judge in St Petersburg, whose comfortable life is interrupted by a pain in his side that will not go away.

people.name: Praskovya Fyodorovna
people.text: Ivan's wife, with whom he lives in polite distance, and who is more concerned with the household's standing than with him.

people.name: Gerasim
people.text: A young peasant servant, cheerful and plain-spoken, who looks after Ivan's body without embarrassment or pretence.

context.title: Retrospective structure
context.text: Death is announced at the beginning rather than saved as a surprise. The central uncertainty concerns the meaning and recognition of the life.
context.takeaway: Read for understanding rather than medical suspense.

context.title: Respectable normality
context.text: Ivan follows recognised models of advancement and taste. The narrative tests whether social approval can establish that a life was well lived.
context.takeaway: Approval is evidence of conformity, not final worth.

notice.why: Classification can displace recognition of a suffering person.
Comfort depends on more than avoiding an awkward truth.

opening: Ivan Ilyich has arranged his life properly: a respectable career, suitable acquaintances, and a home furnished with the right things. When he becomes seriously ill, the people around him continue observing the conventions that have always made life manageable. Their tact becomes unbearable. Tolstoy brings a successful man into a situation where professional standing and tasteful furniture offer no assistance, and where the question of whether he has lived well becomes urgent before he has learned how to ask it honestly.
